messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] how much time will be needed for "mqmaugment"process
parts:
With such a large number of markers and high rate of missing genotypes, mqmaugment is not going to be feasible; it’s trying to expand the rows in the genotype data, with genotypes filled-in in all possible ways. 

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] how much time will be needed for "mqmaugment"process
parts:
A higher minprob won't help much, and if you use fill.geno, you don't need mqmaugment.
But I wouldn't be comfortable using fill.geno with such a high rate of missing data.

I would recommend focusing on multiple imputation or haley-knott regression, and using some of the other functions in R/qtl,
such as scanone, stepwiseqtl, and makeqtl/fitqtl/addqtl.

karl

many thanks for your informative help.

to be honest, I am quite new in this R field. what you mentioned are new and confusing me now. i am not sure in what case what methods should I use to fill those missing data, I only have this "Tutorial Multiple QTL mapping analysis for R/qtl" from top notch published paper, and from which I have got some idea about the process for MQM.

i have got this 40% missing geno data from internet, and got those phnotype measured. what I want  is  which chromosome should i focus on by using R/qtl.

it looks i should use different filling genodata methods not just copy from papers. any possibility you could roughly show me

1,what is the rules for using different filling methods?

2,when should i use scanone scantwo or MQMscan?

or possible tutorials or codes show this process?

with my best regards

ma



在 2018年10月11日星期四 UTC+8下午8:46:15，Karl Broman写道：

A higher minprob won't help much, and if you use fill.geno, you don't need mqmaugment.

I would recommend focusing on multiple imputation or haley-knott regression, and using some of the other functions in R/qtl,
such as scanone, stepwiseqtl, and makeqtl/fitqtl/addqtl.

karl
